title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement: Given a string `s`, return the longest substring of `s` that is a **palindrome** (reads the same forwards and backwards).

example.why: 'bab' is a palindrome of length 3. ('aba' is just as long; this code keeps the first one it finds.)

idea: A palindrome is symmetric around its **centre**. So instead of testing every substring, pick a centre and grow outward as long as the two ends match.
A palindrome of odd length has a letter as its centre (`aba`); one of even length has a gap between two letters as its centre (`abba`). Try both kinds at every position: 2n − 1 centres.
Each expansion stops at the first mismatch (or at the edge of the string). Keep the longest palindrome found.

complexity.timeWhy: 2n − 1 centres, and each expansion can run across the whole string.
complexity.spaceWhy: Every expansion hands back its palindrome as a new string of up to n characters. (Returning the two indexes instead would need only O(1).)

steps.text: Our example: **`s = "babad"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`longest` will hold the longest palindrome found so far.
Centre on the letter `b` (index 0). A single letter is always a palindrome — now grow outward.
The expansion would leave the string → stop. This centre gives `b`.
`b` (length 1) is longer than the best so far → `longest` = `b`.
Centre on the gap between index 0 and 1: `b` ≠ `a`, so there is no even-length palindrome here.
Centre on the letter `a` (index 1). A single letter is always a palindrome — now grow outward.
`s[0]` and `s[2]` are both `b`: the ends match, so `bab` is a palindrome. Grow outward again.
The expansion would leave the string → stop. This centre gives `bab`.
`bab` (length 3) is longer than the best so far → `longest` = `bab`.
Centre on the gap between index 1 and 2: `a` ≠ `b`, so there is no even-length palindrome here.
Centre on the letter `b` (index 2). A single letter is always a palindrome — now grow outward.
`s[1]` and `s[3]` are both `a`: the ends match, so `aba` is a palindrome. Grow outward again.
`s[0]` = `b` and `s[4]` = `d` differ → stop. This centre gives `aba`.
Centre on the gap between index 2 and 3: `b` ≠ `a`, so there is no even-length palindrome here.
Centre on the letter `a` (index 3). A single letter is always a palindrome — now grow outward.
`s[2]` = `b` and `s[4]` = `d` differ → stop. This centre gives `a`.
Centre on the gap between index 3 and 4: `a` ≠ `d`, so there is no even-length palindrome here.
Centre on the letter `d` (index 4). A single letter is always a palindrome — now grow outward.
The expansion would leave the string → stop. This centre gives `d`.
Nothing follows index 4, so there is no even-length centre here.
Every centre has been tried. The longest palindrome is **`bab`**.
Done — the answer is **`"bab"`**. 'bab' is a palindrome of length 3. ('aba' is just as long; this code keeps the first one it finds.)
